title: Grateful Dead Live at Pauley Pavilion, UCLA on 1982-02-21
lineage: Sbd> cassette > dat> cdr> Eac > cool edit pro > shntool > cdwav > shnv3

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with good clarity captures a high‑energy 1982 Pauley Pavilion show featuring a blazing Shakedown, fiery Jerry on “Tiger,” and standout Phil bass on NFA/​Stella Blue, though the missing China Cat Sunflower is a disappointment.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its fire and tight playing – the opening Shakedown‑Minglewood set, Jerry’s scorching “Tiger” solo, Brent’s solid keys, and Phil’s bass bombs on the NFA→Stella Blue segment are repeatedly highlighted.  The soundboard source is described as clear but a bit flat, still plenty listenable, with the only major gripe being the absent China Cat Sunflower.  Overall the show feels high‑energy and memorable despite that omission.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars, emphasizing strong musical performance and generally good soundboard quality; only a few outliers note missing songs or flat mix, so the weighted average is high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners note the tape sounds clear and well‑mixed for an early‑80s SBD, though some describe it as a little flat or lacking bass depth. No major dropouts reported.

poor_songs: China Cat Sunflower (missing from this version)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong, upbeat first set that builds momentum with Shakedown and Minglewood; second set remains solid despite the missing China Cat, highlighted by tight jams on Estimated Prophet through Stella Blue and a satisfying encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for being "on fire," delivering great tone on Tiger and strong lead work throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for “dropping bombs” – powerful, sweet bass especially on the NFA intro/outro into Stella Blue.
band_member_comments.Bob: Celebrated for his rhythm guitar tone and artistic phrasing; several reviewers call him one of the greatest rhythm players.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland receives compliments for solid solos and engaging keyboard work, though a few mention the piano sounding tinny at times.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drum segments are described as tight and well‑executed, providing a good launch into spacey sections.
